sources.name: Here's All the Countries With TikTok Bans - Time

_: Banned from government devices and in certain states
Nationwide ban imposed over national security concerns; no official reversal announced as of 2026
International TikTok blocked; domestic app Douyin used instead

Federal agencies and numerous state governments prohibited TikTok on government-issued devices due to cybersecurity and data security concerns. Many individual states have additional regulations or outright bans.
Eight-day ban; lifted after TikTok pledged content moderation
Four separate ban/lift cycles between Oct 2020 and Nov 2021 over content moderation disputes; fully restored after TikTok assurances
Blocked in 2018 as part of a crackdown on pornography and gambling sites; later restored. Temporarily blocked again during 2024 protests.
Access severely restricted after 2022 Ukraine invasion; uploads limited and content controls applied, with partial access still available via VPNs
Government imposes ongoing content moderation and censorship rules, especially for political and national security-related content; no full nationwide ban reported
Government and public-sector employees prohibited from using TikTok on official devices due to security and data protection concerns
TikTok prohibited on civil servant devices due to cybersecurity, privacy, and misinformation concerns
Federal government banned TikTok on all government-issued devices following security review; similar bans adopted across provincial and territorial governments
Included in personal data violators register; access blocked from Uzbek IP addresses
Nationwide ban introduced due to concerns over social harmony and misuse; lifted in August 2024 after agreement with TikTok on identifying criminal misuse
TikTok banned on all federal government devices, including ministers and agencies, due to cybersecurity concerns following national security review
Ban announced by communications ministry over propaganda and indecent content, but enforcement is inconsistent and users may still access the platform
TikTok blocked during political unrest following arrest of opposition leader; lifting tied to regulatory agreement with government
Government advised suspension in 2022 and ordered removal from official work phones in 2023 due to data protection and security concerns
Federal government prohibited TikTok on federal work devices due to cybersecurity, privacy, and misinformation concerns
Six-day temporary ban in Dec 2022; later reports in 2023 suggested continued restrictions due to compliance issues
National cyber security agency issued warning against TikTok due to cybersecurity, privacy, and influence risks for critical infrastructure and public institutions
Access restricted during the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict; additional restrictions imposed in 2023
Federal government prohibited private use and installation of TikTok on work devices for federal employees based on security service advice
Full consumer ban introduced due to child mental health and content moderation concerns; lifting proposed in Feb 2026, status still unresolved
International TikTok blocked; domestic app Douyin used instead
Ministry of Defence banned TikTok on work devices due to security concerns
National Security Authority advised ban on TikTok for ministers, state secretaries, and political advisors on work devices due to security concerns
National Cyber Security Centre advised that TikTok should not be installed or used on official public sector devices due to security concerns
Parliamentary Service banned TikTok on devices connected to Parliament following cybersecurity advice from the Government Communications Security Bureau
Loss of TikTok functionality reported during the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict; government involvement not confirmed
Nationwide ban introduced for at least one year due to concerns over youth violence; enforcement began in March 2025 and was later lifted after court ruling in 2026
Broad social media restrictions during civil unrest; applied to multiple platforms including TikTok
Ministry of Foreign Affairs banned TikTok on official work devices due to security concerns
TikTok prohibited on state-issued smartphones for public officials; installation removed and blocked on centrally managed devices
Malta Information Technology Agency restricted TikTok on government devices, blocking access unless approved through a controlled internet package
Temporary nationwide restriction imposed by France during civil unrest following election law protests; later lifted
